newsitem.title: USA: U.S. legislator pleads in own drunken driving case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. legislator pleads in own drunken driving case.

text.p: The head of an alcohol and drug abuse committee in New York state who faced drunken driving charges pleaded guilty to a lesser charge on Wednesday and said she had learned from her mistake.

Rochester Assemblywoman Susan John, who sponsored a "zero tolerance" bill to keep teenagers from driving while drunk, agreed to a plea bargain. She was fined $300 for driving while impaired, a violation instead of the harsher misdemeanor, driving while intoxicated.
"I believe that from this mistake, I need to make something positive happen," John, chairwoman of the State Assembly's Alcohol and Drug Abuse committee, told a news conference after her sentencing.
"This will give me additional insights into the problem of drinking and driving, and I believe, will allow me to do my job even more effectively."
John's boss, Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, said he would not ask the Democrat lawmaker, first elected to the Assembly in 1990, to leave her post on the drug and alcohol abuse committee.

Police pulled John over at 1:26 a.m. on Tuesday in the Albany suburb of Colonie when her car was spotted crossing a double yellow line on a two-lane road. Police said her blood alcohol was .14 percent, which is .4 percent above the legal limit.
After her arrest, John admitted she drank and drove and intended to enter a guilty plea and "do whatever the judge tells me to."

In addition to the fine, Town Judge Nicholas Greisler put restrictions on her license for three months and ordered her to attend a drunken driving course and attend a victim impact panel where she will listen to the people who were in drunken driving accidents.

John was scheduled to return to court on March 17 after she was issued three tickets, one for driving while intoxicated, one for driving with a blood alcohol content more than .10 percent and one for crossing the centre line.
The "zero tolerance" bill John sponsored threatens those under 21 who drink and drive with loss of their driver's licenses.
